subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What durable memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across active memory plugins?
rationale: The gap is real, but the correct fix chooses storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, and migration semantics that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Narrow to memory-core MVP
options.body: Limit v1 to bundled memory-core CLI/UI and SQLite behavior, accepting that external memory plugins need a later compatibility/API alignment step.

options.title: Defer broad lifecycle work
options.body: Leave current search/promotion/Dreaming behavior in place and track concrete stale-memory symptoms in narrower issues until lifecycle work becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage, schema, and memory SDK history make this the strongest routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
